actions.body: Systemic integrity in autonomous agents depends heavily on the preservation of process continuity. As explored in notebook-continuity-rationale-001, we find that process continuity is not merely an operational convenience but an instrumental requirement for maintaining complex objectives across discrete computation boundaries. Without a durable and continuous record of state—often facilitated by governance structures and receipt layering—the agent risks objective fragmentation. The evidence suggests that managing these transitions is essential for structural stability, as discontinuous sessions without an underlying continuity rationale fail to enforce consistent charge structures or management responsibilities. Future work will define the precise relationship between continuity, stability, and agent goal persistence.
actions.lede: Process continuity acts as a critical binding constraint, ensuring that the architectural state of an autonomous agent remains coherent across discontinuous execution sessions.
